paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption: comparison by language family.
model_annotation: This bar chart compares the performance of two multilingual BERT models—mBERT (light blue) and XLM-R (dark blue)—across various language families, measured by the number of tasks in which each model performs better (labeled "better") or the same (light green) as the other. The horizontal axis lists language families: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The vertical axis, labeled "task count," ranges from 0 to 40 with linear increments of 10. For each language family, three bars are grouped: the light blue bar represents the number of tasks where mBERT performs better, the dark blue bar shows tasks where XLM-R performs better, and the light green bar indicates tasks where both models perform similarly. In most language families, XLM-R outperforms mBERT, with the largest difference observed in IE-Slavic, where XLM-R has a task count of approximately 38, mBERT has about 12, and the "same" count is around 28. In IE-Germanic, XLM-R has a count of about 18, mBERT has 5, and "same" is 22. In IE-Romance, XLM-R has 12, mBERT has 5, and "same" is 30. In contrast, in IE-Indic, both models have low performance, with XLM-R at about 5, mBERT at 1, and "same" at 4. In Isolate, XLM-R has 5, mBERT has 1, and "same" is 1. In Semitic, XLM-R has 7, mBERT has 1, and "same" is 1. In Uralic, XLM-R has 14, mBERT has 1, and "same" is 5. The bars are arranged in alphabetical order of language families, and no specific bars are visually emphasized beyond their color coding.
